intent.raw: Make the node-card font easier to read and refine the idea that everything is the canvas, with supporting elements inside it and independently minimizable.
intent.objective: Produce an implementation-ready, non-executed design and plan for a canvas-first ontology workspace with readable graph cards and accessible collapsible support panels.
intent.operator_sentence: Refine the idea that everything is the canvas and the other elements are inside it and can be minimized.

route_menu.context_hint: The operator selected a canvas-first direction; the remaining design choice is how support content behaves around the graph.

items.label: Canvas with docked panels
items.description: Keep the graph persistent while explanation, details, and evidence open as collapsible edge panels. Recommended for state continuity and keyboard access.

items.label: Canvas with floating cards
items.description: Allow movable overlay cards. More flexible, but collision, persistence, focus order, and mobile behavior become substantially harder.

items.label: Canvas with modal drawers
items.description: Show one full-height drawer at a time. Simpler on mobile, but weak for comparing explanations and selected-node details on desktop.

gates.condition: REFINE-DISPATCH.json validates before any runtime-backed stage or helper starts.
The operator explicitly confirms the standard ten-stage route and one read-only UX evidence reviewer.
Every stage records an owner-native artifact or explicit blocked reason.
Panel visibility, selection, focus, zoom, and filters remain ephemeral visualization state and never become ontology, memory, routing, or authority state.
Design names card typography, layout, dock states, focus return, mobile single-sheet behavior, and synchronized text alternative.
Refine produces design and plan artifacts only; product implementation requires a separately admitted execution route.

boundaries.contract: No stage or helper starts until the operator confirms the displayed strategy.
The helper receives only the seed and design artifact, remains read-only, and returns a structured UX risk receipt without changing product or evidence files.
Refine may name product edits in a plan but cannot perform or report them as implemented.

state_namespaces.write_policy: Refine and stage owners may write only declared run artifacts after strategy confirmation.
No writes during the Refine route.

promotion_guardrails: Candidate-local visualization only; no routing, runtime, memory, reasoning, authority, release, or production claim.
Refine artifacts are design evidence, not product implementation evidence.
Human visual preference and comprehension remain residue after browser-observable checks.
The concurrent ontology validation receipt is outside this run's write scope.
